$comment: ★★ LANE-CFG EDIT 2/4 — `includes: [{header: windows.h, when: {format: pe}}]`. THIS EDGE IS NOT A CONVENIENCE: IT STATES A DEPENDENCY THAT ALREADY EXISTS IN THE SHIPPED BODY. DSS's own pe realization of this header, `runtime/platform/src/dirent.c`, IS a Win32 implementation — line 62 of that file is `#include <windows.h>`, and the unit drives `_wfindfirst64i32` / `MultiByteToWideChar` / `WideCharToMultiByte` over the Win32 find-file primitives. A pe consumer of <dirent.h> is therefore already, unavoidably, a consumer of the Win32 surface; this edge makes that visible in the descriptor graph instead of leaving it implicit inside a source file. That is what makes it honest rather than expedient. ⚠ ITS MARGINAL IS CONDITIONAL ON EDIT 3, AND THE MEASUREMENT SAYS SO PLAINLY: added to a tree that already carries edits 1+4, this edge closes ZERO of the remaining 65 `fileio.c` errors — without the <direct.h>→<dirent.h> edge this descriptor is never in that TU's closure at all. Leave-one-out from the full set is where its weight shows: dropping it leaves 41 errors. THE TWO EDGES ARE A CHAIN, NOT TWO INDEPENDENT CONTRIBUTORS, and any report that adds their separate marginals is double-counting. | ★★★ THE FIRST AND (this cycle) ONLY SHIPPED-SOURCE REALIZATION — D-RUNTIME-DSS-SHIPS-NO-IMPLEMENTATION-HALF, operator ruling 2026-08-17. `library` says WHICH IMAGE a symbol is imported FROM, per object format; the sibling `realization` map says WHETHER it is imported at all. Windows has no POSIX directory API in ANY platform image — not ucrtbase, not kernel32 — so on `pe` opendir/readdir/closedir are PROVIDED by the shipped source file `src/dss-config/runtime/platform/src/dirent.c` rather than imported, and the driver adds that file to the build graph as an ordinary extra translation unit compiled FOR THE TARGET, on any host, cross. On `elf`/`macho` the map carries no key, so the DEFAULT (import, from `library`) stands and those two arms are byte-identical to the pre-ruling descriptor. ★ NOTE WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT: there is NO `library.pe` here. Naming an image AND a source for one format is refusal R3 — two owners for one body — and the loader REFUSES it (F_ShippedLibDescriptorMalformed) rather than picking one. ★ THE VALUE IS A CONFIG-ROOT-RELATIVE PATH, AND THAT DECISION WAS MADE DELIBERATELY — recorded here so it is not re-litigated. An earlier draft of this axis had the descriptor name a bare UNIT (`{"unit":"dirent"}`) and let a loader convention derive the path, on the argument that a future re-layout should not be a config migration. That was OVERRULED (operator, 2026-08-17) and the reason is stronger than the one it replaced: a derived path means the string in the descriptor is NOT the string you can paste into `ls`, and it is not greppable in either direction — you cannot find the body from the declaration, or the declaration from the body, without knowing the composition rule. A manifest listing units was considered and DELETED for the same family of reason: it would have been a THIRD copy of facts the descriptor and the file tree already own, able to drift from both. So `source` names a FILE, resolved against `src/dss-config/` — the same anchor `findShippedConfig` already resolves every other shipped thing against. Nothing is derived and nothing is composed. The `pe/` segment above the include-namespace mirror (`pe/sys/stat.c` ↔ `sys/stat.json`) exists because JSON can say `when:{format}` and C source cannot: a flat `dirent.c` would sit in the path of whoever next needs an elf body, and the path of least resistance from there is an `#ifdef` inside it. ★★ THE pe `struct dirent` VARIANT BELOW IS NOT DECORATION — the shipped unit `#include`s THIS header, so this declaration is the ONE the implementation compiles against: mutate it and the runtime source stops compiling. The layout agreement is checked by the compiler, not by review. Layout is mingw-w64's (the de-facto POSIX-on-Windows ABI; reference compilers ARE the spec): `long d_ino` (LLP64 ⇒ i32), `unsigned short d_reclen`, `unsigned short d_namlen`, `char d_name[FILENAME_MAX]` with mingw's FILENAME_MAX = 260. d_ino and d_reclen are ALWAYS ZERO there — Win32 exposes neither an inode number nor an on-disk record length — and the unit reproduces that rather than inventing values a caller might trust. | Neutral shipped <dirent.h> (POSIX) — c81 (the sqlite shell.c CLI route; shell.c includes it at 179 + 9840 [fileio.c], both !_WIN32; the static windirent opendir/readdir/closedir defs at 3948-4095 are `_WIN32 && _MSC_VER`-only, inactive here). Surface = shell.c's use: `DIR *pDir` (a fileio struct member) + opendir/readdir/closedir + `struct dirent *pEntry -> pEntry->d_name`. ★ DIR is OPAQUE (glibc: `typedef struct __dirstream DIR` — an INCOMPLETE type; user code only ever holds DIR*, opendir allocates internally): shipped as a typedef to the EMPTY named struct `struct "DIR" opaque` — the exact FILE precedent (stdio.json types FILE* as `ptr<struct "FILE" {}>`), so `DIR *p` resolves in type position (the typedefs surface also seeds the parse-time cast-vs-call oracle) while member access on it stays impossible (no field scope -> fails loud), faithfully opaque. ⚠ THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW REFUTED, so it is restated rather than deleted: it read 'The dir-handle params/returns are ptr<void> per house style (time.json precedent — C void*<->T* coercion; the pointee layout never enters a signature)'. ✔That was a description of a DEFECT wearing the word 'house style' — [[D-FFI-DIRENT-API-DECLARED-OVER-VOID-NOT-ITS-OWN-STRUCTS]], closed P56. The three signatures are now typed over the two types THIS FILE ALREADY DECLARED: opendir :: fn(ptr<char>) -> ptr<DIR>, readdir :: fn(ptr<DIR>) -> ptr<dirent>, closedir :: fn(ptr<DIR>) -> i32. ★★ WHAT MAKES THE `dirent` SPELLING SAFE ACROSS THREE INCOMPATIBLE LAYOUTS: it is a BY-NAME reference resolved against THIS descriptor's own `structs` vocabulary AFTER the per-format variant has been selected, so the elf read binds the 280-byte glibc record, the pe read the 268-byte mingw-w64 one and the macho read the 1048-byte Darwin one — from ONE signature, with no format ever named in it. Spelling the layout INLINE in the signature would have been the fresh defect: one body for three ABIs. ⚠ It required an ordering change in the reader (`structs` now decode BEFORE `symbols`, joining the typedef and union surfaces that already did) — a signature could not name a struct at all until P56. ★ A TARGET-LESS read (LSP / direct API / the AllShippedDescriptorsDecode sweep) selects NO variant, and there the tag is published INCOMPLETE, so `ptr<dirent>` is still a well-formed pointer and the read still states no per-target fact it cannot know. `ptr<char>` on opendir stays UNANNOTATED deliberately — POSIX spells it `const char *`, but an unannotated row makes NO qualifier claim (D-CSUBSET-SUPPRESSED-SHIPPED-ROW-SIGNATURE-UNCHECKED's over-reach detector), and annotating three rows out of ~1500 would be an inconsistency, not a fix. ★ struct dirent IS layout-critical (readdir returns libc's own struct; shell.c reads d_name at its glibc offset): verified against the REAL /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/bits/dirent.h AND the aarch64 cross headers in WSL (IDENTICAL, LP64, non-__USE_FILE_OFFSET64 default): d_ino __ino_t(u64) @0, d_off __off_t(i64) @8, d_reclen unsigned short(u16) @16, d_type unsigned char(u8) @18, d_name char[256] @19 -> sizeof 280 (derived: 275 padded to 8-align); the layout engine derives exactly these offsets. ★ c117 (the macho shell.c CLI leg, user §B): the Darwin variant lands — the 64-bit-inode struct dirent (verified against the real macOS SDK sys/dirent.h `__DARWIN_STRUCT_DIRENTRY`, the arm64 default): d_ino u64 @0, d_seekoff u64 @8, d_reclen u16 @16, d_namlen u16 @18, d_type u8 @20, d_name char[1024] @21 -> sizeof 1048 (vs the glibc 280B / d_name@19); shell.c reads d_name, so a single layout would read the wrong bytes. SYMBOLS: on arm64-darwin the 64-bit-inode ABI is the ONLY ABI, so opendir/readdir/closedir are the PLAIN names (NO `$INODE64` suffix). ★★ TF-C121 (D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME) — opendir/readdir now carry a per-arch `linkName`, and the sentence replaced here was WRONG: it called the x86_64 `readdir$INODE64` alias 'a documented no-consumer residual', which reads as harmless. It is not harmless and it is not loud — it is a LATENT instance of the exact silent misbinding sys/stat.json's fstat had. This file declares the MODERN 1048-byte `struct dirent` with d_name@21; the legacy 32-bit-inode `_readdir` returns the OLD one with d_name@8, so every x86_64 directory walk would read garbage names out of the middle of d_ino/d_seekoff. It never fails loud, because a descriptor SHADOWS the SDK header entirely (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp: Descriptor beats Source) — the SDK's `__DARWIN_ALIAS_I` asm label never participates, and libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH spellings, so the plain-name import resolves. MEASURED, matched two-arch control on macOS 26.5.2 (ONE TU, only `-arch` differs): x86_64 `cc` emits `_opendir$INODE64`/`_readdir$INODE64`, arm64 emits `_opendir`/`_readdir`; `closedir` is PLAIN on both (it takes no inode-shaped struct — it is the control that proves this is per-symbol, not per-header). This pair was found by compiling all 246 shipped imports for both arches and DIFFING the emitted link names — a header grep had missed `opendir`, which routes through `__DARWIN_ALIAS_I` rather than `__DARWIN_INODE64`. Unexercised today; fixed anyway, because it is the same defect. `linkName` declares the UNDECORATED base — the Mach-O `_` is composed by the engine. libc symbols verified: opendir/readdir/closedir @GLIBC_2.2.5 (libc.so.6) / _opendir/_readdir/_closedir (libSystem).
